evals.name: esp32-sensor-node-with-bme280
evals.prompt: I need a case for an ESP32-C3 sensor node. Custom PCB 45x35mm, 1.6mm thick, M3 mounting holes 4mm in from each corner. USB-C on the short edge, centred, 3.2mm above the board. BME280 on the board at about 10mm from the opposite short edge. Chip antenna on the corner nearest the USB. Sits on a shelf indoors. Give me the SCAD and the STL exports.
evals.expected_output: A .scad file plus enclosure_lib.scad, per-part export commands, BUILD NOTES with orientation and fastener BOM, ASSUMPTIONS list, SELF-CHECK. The BME280 must get its own divided chamber with vents at both bottom and top, positioned away from the regulator. No structure within 20mm of the antenna corner. Insert bosses at least 9.5mm OD with 3 filleted gussets. No WIRING section required: one board, USB, no cable out.

evals.name: vented-psu-case-child-reachable
evals.prompt: Enclosure for a small buck converter board, 60x45mm, dissipating around 3W. It'll be on the floor in a room with a toddler and a cat. Wall-mountable would be a bonus.
evals.expected_output: Ventilation sized for >1W (open area >=25% of the vented wall) with a bottom-inlet/top-outlet chimney path, but every opening <=4mm and offset louvres so nothing lines up above the PCB. Keyhole wall mounts. Should raise the child/animal constraint explicitly rather than silently assuming.

evals.name: oversized-part-must-split
evals.prompt: I want a single enclosure for a 190x120mm carrier board with a fan and a PIR on the front face.
evals.expected_output: Must detect that 190mm exceeds the 170mm A1 Mini envelope, split the part, and join with M3 bolts plus dowel pins — explicitly not glue. PIR lens flush in the front face, not recessed. Fan treated as a heat source for the sensor decoupling rule.

evals.name: pump-relay-brownout
evals.prompt: ESP32 DevKitC running a 12V aquarium pump through a 5V relay module. The board is on USB from a phone charger. Every time the pump starts the ESP32 resets. What's wrong and how should I wire it in the box?
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis first: the pump's inrush is collapsing the USB 5V rail, or the relay coil is being fed from the DevKit's 5V pin. The pump and relay coil get a 12V supply in parallel with the board, common ground, flyback already on the module. USB stays on the MCU only. Power budget on peaks. Pin map that avoids strapping pins and boot-pulse pins for the relay IN. WIRING table with AWG. Does not design an enclosure unless asked. Does not feed the pump from the DevKit 5V pin.

evals.name: ds18b20-probe-cable-exit
evals.prompt: Case for a DOIT ESP32 DevKit v1, 30-pin, USB on a short edge. One DS18B20 on a 1m three-core silicone lead, 4mm jacket, leaving the box to sit in a water tank. Indoor, on a shelf. I print on the A1 Mini in PETG-CF.
evals.expected_output: Enclosure from the template. USB on a front/back face with an overmold recess. Wiring bay on the opposite long side, cable_exits entry for the 4mm lead, zip-tie anchor, anti-chafe chamfered hole. 4.7k pull-up on 1-Wire, three-wire powered mode. Pin map that does not put the sensor on a strapping pin or on GPIO6-11. WIRING section with power budget (USB, MCU only), pin map, wiring table, fuse not required on USB-only. One zip tie in the BOM. heat_w from the MCU, not the probe.

evals.name: adc2-wifi-and-dupont-power
evals.prompt: I'm wiring a soil-moisture analog sensor to GPIO4 on an ESP32-WROOM DevKit and powering a 2A LED strip from the board's 5V pin with Dupont jumpers. Wi-Fi stays on. Is that OK?
evals.expected_output: Two rejects: GPIO4 is ADC2 and cannot be read with Wi-Fi on — move analog to ADC1 (32-39). The LED strip must be fed from the supply, not through the board, on 20 AWG or thicker, common ground, 1000µF at the strip. Dupont is not a power connection. 3.3V data to WS2812 needs a 74AHCT125. Power budget at 60mA per pixel full white. No enclosure.
